final_report.summary: Across 2 cycles, the AI-StoryForge project was transformed from a sequential research pipeline with an overly generous 3-credit signup system into a concurrent, Haiku-powered research engine with a carefully gated freebie token system. Cycle 1 built the core infrastructure: concurrent research via asyncio.gather() in stage_research.py, the credit/transaction system in database/models.py, freebie detection logic in web/routes.py, genre restriction with 5 safe genres in data/free_genres.json, and the UI tier differentiation in app.html. Cycle 2 polished the experience: fixed 7 test assertions in test_round2.py to accept HTTP 422 (FastAPI's actual validation response), enhanced the UI with a SAMPLE badge, Haiku banner, and tier comparison table, verified concurrent research end-to-end, documented the sample vs regular token contrast, and validated the complete credit flow journey from signup through credit exhaustion. All 153 tests pass across 3 test files.
key_achievements: Concurrent research pipeline using asyncio.gather() - genre and psychology research run in parallel on Haiku subagents, reducing latency from ~0.60s to ~0.20s
Freebie token system: 1 free credit on signup, restricted to 5 safe genres (no erotic/romance), Haiku-only, SAMPLE watermark on all outputs
Server-side genre and model enforcement prevents all bypass attempts (genre injection, model override, double-spend via concurrent requests)
Clear UI tier differentiation: SAMPLE badge, 'Running on Haiku' banner, tier comparison table contrasting sample (1 genre/5 safe/Haiku) vs regular (4 genres/72 full catalog/full model)
153 tests passing across 3 test files covering functional, adversarial, UI verification, and concurrent research validation
Atomic credit deduction with transaction logging prevents double-spend even under concurrent request pressure
Fixed 7 adversarial test assertions to match FastAPI's actual 422 validation response codes
challenges_overcome: HTTP 422 vs 400 status code discrepancy - FastAPI returns 422 for validation errors by default, not 400. Tests needed updating to match actual framework behavior.
Freebie detection logic - distinguishing users who only have signup bonus credits from users who purchased credits required inspecting the full transaction history
Double-spend prevention - ensuring atomic credit deduction under concurrent request pressure required SQL-level atomicity (UPDATE ... WHERE credits > 0)
Genre bypass prevention - server-side validation needed to reject restricted genres even if the client sends them directly, covering all edge cases
lessons_learned: Always verify framework-specific HTTP status codes (FastAPI uses 422 for validation, not 400) before writing test assertions
Server-side validation is mandatory for any restriction - UI-only restrictions are trivially bypassable
Atomic database operations (single UPDATE with WHERE clause) are simpler and more reliable than check-then-update patterns for credit systems
asyncio.gather() with return_exceptions=True is the cleanest pattern for concurrent API calls - isolates per-task failures without killing the batch
UI tier communication works best with side-by-side comparison tables rather than just hiding features from restricted users
